summary: Changes the IANA registration procedure for the IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry, which RFC 5029 created, from Standards Action to Expert Review. This makes it easier to allocate new bit values. It updates RFC 5029.

eli5.summary: There is a list of special labels that routers can stick on links. Before, adding a label needed a big formal approval. Now a few experts can say yes, which is quicker.

questions: how to register is-is neighbor link attribute bits
is-is link attribute sub-tlv registry procedure
subtitle: Relaxes approval rules for IS-IS neighbor link attribute bit registration.

tldr.problem: RFC 5029 required Standards Action (full RFC process) to register new IS-IS neighbor link attribute bits, which was too restrictive for experimental and vendor-specific extensions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9650 changes the registration procedure from Standards Action to Expert Review, allowing qualified experts to approve new bits without an RFC, reducing delays.
tldr.outcome: IS-IS implementations can more quickly deploy new link attributes for experimental use or vendor extensions while maintaining security and avoiding collisions.

today: RFC 9650 is the current standard governing allocation of new IS-IS link attribute bits. Operators and vendors needing new bits should follow its Expert Review process.

sections.title: Link Attributes in IS-IS
sections.content:
IS-IS is a routing protocol where routers exchange information about the network topology. RFC 5029 defined a way to attach attributes to links between routers, using individual bit flags in a Sub-TLV. For example, a link might be marked as restricted, or as having special properties for traffic engineering.

When new attributes are needed (for experiments, vendor extensions, or future standards), they require a new bit value. RFC 5029 mandated that any new bit allocation go through Standards Action, the same process required for new RFCs.
sections.eli5: Routers tag their connections with flags. Adding a new flag type required starting a whole RFC process.

sections.title: Expert Review Process
sections.content:
RFC 9650 changes the allocation procedure to Expert Review. Under this policy, IANA consults with designated experts in IS-IS routing to evaluate requests for new bits. The experts check that the request is valid and that the bit value doesn't collide with other uses, but they do not require the work to be published as an RFC.

RFC 7370 and RFC 5029 provide guidance to experts reviewing such requests, ensuring that allocations are sensible and follow IS-IS conventions.
sections.eli5: Instead of writing an RFC, you ask a few experts. They check if your idea makes sense and if the number is free, then say yes or no.

sections.title: Enabling Experimentation
sections.content: This change unblocks IS-IS experimentation. Vendors can now quickly reserve bits for proprietary extensions or novel traffic-engineering features. Networks can test new ideas without waiting for standardization. The Standards Action track remains available for mature features that need full RFC treatment.
sections.eli5: Teams trying new router features no longer have to wait years for approval. Once an idea proves itself, it can be formalized later if needed.
